issues.title: Normalized indicator does not shut off in general smooth regions

failure_location.quote:
This
parameter is a smooth function of a local indicator of the
finite-volume update magnitude, and it takes values near zero in smooth
or near-steady regions, and values near one when small cells are active
and SRD is needed to control stiffness.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the blending parameter is near zero in smooth or near-steady regions. The old formula actually establishes exact shut-off only at zero update, and small s_j only when the update is sufficiently small relative to epsilon and tau. A smooth traveling profile can have Delta U_max much larger than epsilon, giving eta_j approximately one and s_j approximately 1/(1+tau^p), about 0.99 for the defaults. Thus generic smooth active regions receive essentially full SRD rather than the advertised shut-off.
issues.overall_effect: Claims that the normalized implementation recovers the base method or avoids SRD dissipation throughout generic smooth regions are unsupported. Exact zero-update steady-state preservation remains valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the self-normalizing operational indicator by the fixed-scale or unnormalized indicator already analyzed in the old source, for example z_j = ΔU_max,j/U_ref with U_ref independent of the current update and s_j = z_j^p/(z_j^p+τ^p). Recalibrate the threshold and update the algorithm, parameter guidance, and activation-dependent experiments consistently. Smooth CFL-scaled updates then give s_j = O(h^p), while exact zero updates still give s_j=0; the conservation and TVD arguments requiring only 0≤s_j≤1 remain applicable.
issues.why_classification: The displayed normalized formula makes the advertised generic smooth-region shut-off genuinely false, so this is neither transcriptional nor a no-loss prose correction. However, the old source already supplies the unnormalized construction and its O(h^p) scaling argument. Operationalizing that construction is a contained but nontrivial redesign and revalidation, not global proof reconstruction or major mathematical loss, so the issue is moderate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
The 
shut-off mechanism is active when finite-volume updates vanish or nearly 
vanish; in fully active advection UM-SRD reduces to standard SRD by design.

issues.title: Arbitrarily-small-cell stability

failure_location.quote:
The instability never progresses
because the large update that would cause it is precisely what triggers
the indicator to re-engage SRD.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that a large unstable update necessarily re-engages enough SRD to prevent the instability. For a neighboring-state difference d that is nonzero, the raw small-cell update contains -(nu/alpha)d. As alpha tends to zero, eta_j tends to one, but for fixed tau the unsmoothed weight tends to 1-s_j = tau^p/(1+tau^p) > 0. The SRD average remains bounded because the small-cell state is volume-weighted by O(alpha), while the identity contribution retains -(1-s_j)(nu/alpha)d. Thus near-full activation does not establish stability uniformly over arbitrarily small alpha.
issues.overall_effect: The old categorical stability explanation and its arbitrary-small-cell consequence are unsupported. The alpha = 0.05 experiment remains numerical evidence for that specified case, not a uniform full-mesh-timestep guarantee.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce an exact stability-safety branch: retain s_j=0 when ΔU_max,j=0, but set s_j=1 whenever ΔU_max,j>0 and the neighborhood's raw local CFL exceeds one; retain the smooth blend only in locally CFL-stable neighborhoods. The dangerous branch is then exactly the weighted-SRD update whose stability is already established in its stated model class, while the zero-update branch makes no change. Add the contained switching/TVD argument and align the smoothness and implementation claims with this branch.
issues.why_classification: For the old activation function, the positive limiting identity weight leaves an O(1/α) contribution, so the categorical stability explanation cannot be repaired by routine wording. Nevertheless, exact safety saturation is a concrete local construction that preserves arbitrary-small-cell stability in the established SRD setting and exact zero-update shut-off. It requires a new contained argument and gives up smooth partial activation only in the unstable-CFL branch, a limited rather than major loss; therefore the issue is moderate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
Extending the TVD and convergence theory to multiple small 
cells, general merging patterns, and multidimensional neighborhood 
topologies remains open, as does a rigorous stability proof for the 
full-mesh timestep regime.

issues.title: Guard parameter incorrectly declared behaviorally irrelevant

failure_location.quote:
This value has no effect on the shut-off
behavior and does not require tuning.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that epsilon has no effect on shut-off behavior and requires no tuning. But eta_j = Delta U_max/(epsilon+Delta U_max); for example, at Delta U_max = epsilon, eta_j = 1/2, and changing epsilon while holding the update fixed changes eta_j. Since s_j is strictly increasing in eta_j, its computed activation changes as well. Epsilon is negligible only when updates are much larger than it, not behaviorally irrelevant in general.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm remains well-defined, but the old parameter guidance incorrectly hides the role of epsilon in setting the near-zero activation scale.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the parameter guidance by stating that ε both prevents a zero denominator and sets the absolute near-zero activation scale: η_j=1/2 when ΔU_max,j=ε, and changing ε changes s_j whenever updates are comparable to ε. Specify that ε is negligible only when relevant nonzero updates are much larger than it and should be chosen relative to the numerical noise or update scale.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine mathematical error in the parameter guidance, not a transcriptional typo, because the reader must check the dependence through both η_j and s_j. The correction is short, local, and routine and leaves the algorithm, proofs, rates, and substantive guarantees unchanged, so it is minor.
